title: Routine Graph
description: A declarative graph agent compiled into a LangGraph runnable by app.progenitor.routines.factory. Backs the Routines page's per-agent execution graph, stored as the agent's 'graph' document (see app/backend/agent_store.py).

entry.description: Node id the compiled graph enters after its private seed node. __seed__ and __project_output__ are reserved for the compiler.

settings.description: Graph-wide options read by app.progenitor.routines.factory.compile_routine_graph. Free-form (a node's own config always wins for anything it declares), but these keys are the ones the compiler actually acts on.

retry.description: Default retry policy applied to every node via StateGraph.set_node_defaults() -- a node's own config.retry overrides this for that node.

recursion_limit.description: Caps LangGraph super-steps (compiled.with_config({'recursion_limit': ...})). The real backstop for a graph cycle: a router-edge loop that never reaches END would otherwise run until this raises GraphRecursionError.

cache.description: Enables an in-memory node-result cache shared by nodes that set their own config.cache.

input_schema.description: Flat field-name -> type-name map (the type name is documentation only, never enforced). Each field becomes a real top-level graph input channel alongside 'messages': a caller can invoke with {"messages": [...], "<field>": <value>}, and the compiler copies each declared field's value into data.<field> before the graph runs, so node config.inputs paths and prompt templates can reference it. 'messages' is always accepted regardless of what's declared here.

output_schema.description: Flat field-name -> type-name map. Each field is resolved as a dotted path against the final 'data' (see routerEdge.state_key for the same dotted-path convention) and returned as a top-level output channel; fields absent from 'data' at the end of the run are silently omitted rather than erroring. Declaring this makes the compiled graph's invoke() return ONLY {"messages": [...], <declared fields>} instead of the full internal state -- everything else (including 'data' itself) is dropped, matching LangGraph's own output_schema projection. 'messages' is always included regardless of what's declared here.

$defs.description: Named JSON Schema definitions reusable across this graph's own node configs (distinct from this meta-schema's own top-level $defs below, which describes node/edge shapes, not routine-authored content). A prompt/eval node's config.response_schema may be {"$ref": "#/$defs/<name>"} instead of repeating an inline schema; app.progenitor.routines.factory.compile_routine_graph resolves the reference against this map before binding model.with_structured_output(...).

nodeId.description: User-defined node id. __seed__ and __project_output__ are reserved for the compiler's private seed/output-projection nodes.

response_schema.description: A raw JSON Schema (object-rooted, per OpenAI Structured Outputs' requirement) for the model's reply, or {"$ref": "#/$defs/<name>"} pointing at a schema declared in this graph's own top-level $defs. When set, the node calls model.with_structured_output(response_schema, method='json_schema', strict=True) instead of a plain invoke -- generation is schema-constrained via the Responses API, not text-parsed after the fact. The validated result becomes data[output_key] directly (a dict, not a string), and no <output_key>_json fallback is produced.

inputs.description: local name -> dotted 'data' path, resolved before evaluation.

rubric_prompt.description: Used only when neither expression nor expression_file is set: the model is asked this. Without response_schema, a reply beginning (case-insensitively) with 'true' evaluates true. With response_schema, the parsed reply's 'result' field (must be boolean) is used instead.

response_schema.description: A raw JSON Schema (object-rooted) for rubric_prompt's reply, with a required boolean 'result' property, or {"$ref": "#/$defs/<name>"} pointing at a schema declared in this graph's own top-level $defs. When set, the node calls model.with_structured_output(response_schema, method='json_schema', strict=True) instead of a plain invoke plus text-prefix heuristic; data[output_key] becomes bool(parsed['result']).

Optional JSON Schema for the agent's final response, or {"$ref": "#/$defs/<name>"} pointing at this graph's top-level $defs. When absent, the final response is stored as data[output_key] text (with a best-effort <output_key>_json object). When set, the final response must be a JSON object satisfying this schema; the validated object is stored directly in data[output_key] and no fallback is produced.

state_key.description: Dotted path read from 'data' after the source node's update is merged.

retryPolicy.description: Fields for langgraph.types.RetryPolicy. The compiler always retries on any exception (retry_on is not configurable here), so this only tunes attempt count and backoff.

max_attempts.description: Total attempts including the first, before the exception propagates. Default 3.

initial_interval.description: Seconds before the first retry. Default 0.1.

backoff_factor.description: Multiplier applied to the interval after each retry. Default 2.0.

max_interval.description: Upper bound on the backoff interval, in seconds. Default 5.0.

jitter.description: Randomize backoff timing to avoid thundering-herd retries. Default false.
